correctness.rationale: The pair invariant proves that homogeneous edges never change; each mixed edge has one eligible vertex while the hub retains its bit. The hub appears at uniform rank among the j mixed-edge resolutions, switches iff rank is at most b-a, and cannot switch twice. This yields the complete labeled kernel and its normalization; multinomial summation yields p_k, a separate beta-integral identity yields c_k, and a triangular-array CLT plus uniform-integrability bounds gives sqrt(pi k)p_k -> 1. Exhaustive exact rational recursion for 10,920 labeled starting states, k=1..6, matches every terminal mass, and a separate independent implementation checks binomial formulas through k=160. Finite checks support but do not replace the all-size argument.

value.rationale: The object is a natural hub-and-disjoint-pairs social graph. It is useful to know how stochastic update order selects among many absorbing states, beyond mere reachability; the full labelled kernel answers that question for arbitrary initial states. The derived square-root probability of a permanent hub switch and exponentially small full-consensus probability exhibit two distinct natural fixation scales, and the all-size exact formulas allow quantitative comparison of local leadership and global unanimity. The result is not a textbook implication of finite-system convergence, nor an arbitrary numerical slice.
